rationale: PINS the declared-type reference graph (#419 section A/B): fields, params, locals, catch unions, and throws clauses each emit References to every named type; generics expand to base + arguments; scoped names stay dotted; primitives silent. M37.21 C9: method RETURN types now also emit declared_type references (TypeUsageGraph->R below via declaredOn=return_type), so the old forbid on R was lifted when returns joined the graph. JD-J12 (M60 java deep review, 2026-09-27): adds the two positions no java fixture pinned. array_creation (`new Gadget[3]`, JLS 15.10.1) was undetectable by the differential — measured 100% subsumed: every one of its 25 corpus edges names a target another rule also names in the same file, so set-based per-file matching cannot see it lost, and no fixture covered it either. The cast expectation plus its forbid pin the JD-J12 spelling fix: an array-wrapped generic cast published `Sprocket<?>` where every other position publishes `Sprocket`. JD-J15 (M60 java deep review, 2026-09-27): an interface CONSTANT is a `constant_declaration` in this grammar, and the branch that created the Constant symbol stored the type on it without emitting a References edge — so an interface's public constants contributed nothing to the type-usage graph while every neighbouring position did. Found by the differential, not by a fixture: it was the last two MISSING rows at 400 files, both ubiquitous types on interface constants.
